answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy works like an orchard tended over seasons: every identity starts as one sapling with limited trust and must earn standing through attested work, the way roots deepen year after year. Reputation sticks to a single continuous record, so spawning a hundred fresh identities means planting a hundred separate orchards from scratch — expensive, slow, and easy to spot — while honest agents ride the rising tide of their cheap, verifiable history instead of spiraling into throwaway accounts chasing quick rewards.
